paragraphs: I am Lily, and I make a birthday card for Grandma. Grandma's birthday is on Sunday. Grandma likes to cook, so I choose a kitchen design. Mom comes to my room and looks at the card. "What is on it?" she asks. "Let me describe it," I say. The card is square, and it is bright yellow. It is small, and it fits in an envelope. I draw it with colored pens.

On the front, there is a funny cartoon cook. He has a very long black beard and a tall white hat. He stands next to a big green cooker. He looks happy, and he holds a spoon. A round blue pot is on the cooker. Pip sits on the kitchen floor. Pip is in my drawing because he likes the kitchen. He pulls a small plastic bag with his teeth. The bag is red, and it is very funny.

"Where is the tab?" asks Mom. "It is at the bottom of the card," I say. "It is a long blue paper tab." "Pull it slowly, and look at the beard!" Mom pulls the tab. She pulls it slowly. The cook's beard grows longer and longer. Mom is surprised, and she laughs. She says it is a very clever card. At the end, there are words on the beard: "Happy Birthday, Grandma!"

Mom laughs and says, "I like the design." "Grandma will love it." I put the card in a yellow envelope. Pip sits next to me and wags his tail. "Woof!" he says. I give him a little hug. "Thank you for the funny idea, Pip," I say.
text.summary: Lily makes a birthday card for Grandma. She describes its color, shape, and design, and she shows how the pull tab makes a funny cook's beard grow long.
